verdict.rationale: SavvyCal's own docs describe registrable webhooks that deliver HTTP POST notifications on account changes. They cover setup under Settings > Integrations, a named event type (event.created), SHA-256 HMAC signing, retries with exponential backoff up to 20 attempts, and a per-webhook request log. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that webhook delivery works as documented, and a complete event catalog beyond event.created.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Webhooks allow you to listen for changes in a SavvyCal account and get notified via HTTP POST requests.
Navigate to Settings > Integrations and click the + icon in the Webhooks
event.created Emitted when someone schedules a new event via one of your scheduling links
SavvyCal signs the request body with a SHA-256 HMAC signature. The signature is included in the x-savvycal-signature header.
we will retry with exponential backoff, up to 20 attempts in all. To see each attempt with its request payload and your response, use the webhook's request log.
